Security & Custody

Emergency Patches and Node Breaches Test Custody

NGINX2Root forces an emergency BTCPay Server patch as a Contabo-hosted Samourai fundraiser node is drained and Trezor discloses a 27,000-order shipping leak.

Compiled from Bitcoin News, TFTC, and Sebastix

Self-hosted payment operators and hardware-wallet buyers spent the past twenty-four hours auditing their exposure after a cluster of infrastructure failures hit the network. BTCPay Server issued an emergency release to patch five newly disclosed nginx vulnerabilities dubbed “NGINX2Root,” warning that the most severe flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution via HTTP/2 and full root compromise when chained with a Linux kernel bug [s358]. Researchers reported that 98.9% of identifiable nginx servers run affected versions, prompting BTCPay Server to state: We're releasing an emergency update to address nginx CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123634, CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-113425. [s358] Sebastix also flagged the advisory alongside fresh Drupal security updates [s144, s83].

Hosting risk turned into direct loss for organizers of the #FREESAMOURAI charity prize draw, who cancelled this weekend’s event after their LND Lightning node was compromised [s360]. Organizer RMessitt wrote that the Contabo-hosted node had strong offline credentials and non-SMS 2FA, yet Our LND node was compromised late last night and the attacker was able to close our lightning channels and sweep the funds held there. [s360] Because Contabo suffered a cyberattack last week, organizers are investigating a link; donated prize-pot funds were unaffected and are being returned, while RMessitt pledged an additional 1M sats to the Samourai Defence Fund [s360].

Physical opsec took a hit as well. Trezor disclosed its third partner data breach in just over three months after hackers compromised shipping partner Skladon on November 7 and likely exported roughly 27,000 order records dating back to August 9 [s298]. No seeds or PINs were exposed, but names, phone numbers, home addresses, and order contents leaked, and customers have already reported fraudulent calls [s298]. Meanwhile, Arkham data showed wallets tied to the $387.5M Bitget breach sending 2,173.76 BTC into CoinJoin transactions over eleven days [s306], and a Scottish hacker linked to Scattered Spider received a six-year prison sentence for an $11.6M crypto theft [s476].

Against a backdrop of U.S. air-traffic groundings, Chase delays, and an NSA network disruption, TFTC argued that outages and cyber headlines are increasingly used to justify surveillance and model restrictions: When someone says safety requires monitoring everything you do, laugh at them. [s467]

Courts & Capital

Leipzig Judge Floats 40,000 BTC Deal in Movie2K Case; Miners Sell Into AI

German prosecutors confirm a settlement offer that would leave the defendant with 16,000 BTC, while public miners liquidate reserves.

A Leipzig judge has offered to drop money-laundering and tax-evasion charges against the alleged operator of piracy site Movie2K if he surrenders 40,000 BTC—worth roughly $2.6 billion—and pays $42 million in compensation, with the trial set to resume December 3 [s339, s468]. Having already sold roughly 50,000 seized coins from the case in mid-2024, state authorities could leave the defendant with an estimated 16,000 BTC if the deal closes [s339, s468].

On the corporate side, listed Bitcoin miners have sold nearly half their holdings since January to finance AI data-center buildouts, led by MARA’s sale of 40,581 BTC for $3.03 billion at an average price of $74,446 [s308]. At the same time, VanEck’s Matthew Sigel described Anthropic’s $1.4 trillion IPO—expected to trade on Nasdaq on November 19 after raising up to $64.35B—as a “capital vacuum” reminiscent of SpaceX’s listing, noting: If the pattern holds, the near-term low may still be ahead in early December, [s388] Even so, Q3 filings showed Wells Fargo expanding its spot Bitcoin ETF holdings to 30.6K BTC and Bank of America growing its stake sevenfold [s347], while Abra Credit tapped ICE Digital Trust to hold segregated Bitcoin collateral for institutional dollar loans [s201].

The AI Buildout

Trillion-Dollar Clones and Zero-Moat Math

Contra & Vitor Pamplona

In a long-form analysis comparing today’s AI data-center debt to the 2008 housing buildup, Contra argued that open-weight replication and zero switching costs are collapsing model margins toward the cost of electricity [s466].

Instead of a winner-take-all market, the AI industry has engineered the most expensive clone factory in corporate history.

With hyperscalers, AI labs, and chipmakers recycling capital through vendor financing, Contra warned that a 20% trim in server budgets could reverse the loop [s466]. Vitor Pamplona underscored the hardware concentration behind the boom, noting Nvidia’s $65.3 billion in single-quarter profit amounts to an Anthropic-sized IPO every three months without selling a share [s334].

Sovereign Stack & Protocol Craft

Code, anti-scraper PoW, and routing around DNS
Dependencies

Magpie Moves Maven Artifacts onto Nostr

Vitor Pamplona

After Maven Central rate-limited his libraries, Vitor Pamplona unveiled Magpie to Ship and fetch Android, Kotlin, and Java dependencies directly over Nostr and Blossom—censorship-resistant, rate-limit-free, and ready for any Gradle build. [s352] Release metadata is signed by the developer’s key, routed via outbox relays, and mirrored across Blossom servers for Quartz and Android builds [s352].

Web Defense

PoWned Makes Crawlers Mine to Read

Printer

When a residential-proxy scraper firing 10,000 rotating IPs dragged page loads from 0.3s to 25s, Printer built PoWned—a WordPress plugin requiring double SHA-256 proof of work before serving expensive filter routes [s221]. In its first hour on gobrrr.me, 31,800 bot requests collapsed within 45 minutes: The bot does 260,000 hashes, the server does three. [s221]

Transport & Identity

TollGate’s Payment Journal and Nostr Navigator

TollGate & lostcause

Ahead of Saturday’s community call, TollGate detailed 158 commits since v0.6.0, adding a durable payment journal and NWC/LNbits wallet support across its Go and Rust router stacks [s12]. Separately, lostcause outlined Nostr Navigator (ncc-browser) to replace DNS and certificate authorities with NCC-05 locators and SPKI pinning, arguing: If your app can be killed by a domain registrar freeze or a revoked TLS cert, it isn't sovereign. [s475]
